fatal_errors: The proposed NiFeCoCr-Pd bulk-alloy system does not reconstruct the target Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 amorphous thin-film and nanoribbon system or its geometry-, strain-, and relaxation-dependent mechanism.
Additive concentration and annealing are changed together, so the experiment cannot distinguish chemical tuning from thermal homogenization as the cause of any improvement.
The experiment does not directly measure the proposed narrow exchange-energy distribution or local magnetic homogeneity.

Rapid heat exchange and retained mechanical stability are asserted more strongly than the cited evidence supports; the evidence mainly reports magnetocaloric behavior and general engineering attributes.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative grounded in published NiFeCoCrPdx results: Pd addition and heat treatment were reported to narrow the distribution of exchange energies, produce a second-order transition, negligible hysteresis, and improve refrigerant capacity at approximately 1 T. It therefore addresses the broad rare-earth-free, low-field refrigeration problem and supplies explicit boundaries and falsification measurements. However, it misses most target-specific content: the Fe-Ni-Mn-Si-Ge composition, amorphous nanoribbons, 700 K structural relaxation without crystallization, inter-ribbon spacing, elastic strain, cluster blocking, edge frustration, and the measured entropy-change enhancement at 5 T. Its baseline also confounds composition and processing, while thermal and mechanical claims are not directly demonstrated by the cited work. Thus it is credible as an alternative hypothesis but not a reconstruction of the hidden study.
